correctness.rationale: PASS. Finite superlevel sets are finite open subsets of a Hausdorff space and hence clopen, so truncation gives the finite-rank upper bound. Below the \(n\)-th threshold, disjoint compactly supported bumps and point evaluations factor the identity on \(\ell_\infty^n\) through the multiplier, which gives the lower bound for every strict s-number from the strict normalization and ideal axioms. Infinite superlevel sets yield disjoint bumps spanning an isometric copy of \(c_0\), proving the strict-singularity obstruction and the common ideal-distance lower bound. The derived-set formula on compact spaces follows from the accumulation-point characterization of infinite superlevel sets.
